title: Isolation of five different primary cell types from a single sample of human skin
protocol: Thaw 0.5 mL liberase aliquot and mix it with 4.5 mL of cold CnT and double concentration of antibiotics in a 15 mL tube.
Empty tissue and transport media into sterile 10 cm plate.
Cut down the midline of the foreskin to open it to a single sheet using sterile scissors and forceps.
Remove large blood clots from the tissue, if present.
Trim any fat deposits from the dermis layer completely using sterile scissors and forceps.
Collect trimmed fat into a tube and add tissue transport medium to keep the fat submerged.
Store the collected fat at 4°C.
Cut the adult tissue into pieces of 5–6 mm² using sterile scissors and forceps.
Cut tissue pieces into strips no more than 7 mm in diameter for efficient liberase penetration.
Transfer the tissue pieces into a 15 mL tube containing liberase solution and invert gently.
Incubate the tissue for 16-20 hours at 4°C with the tube lying on its side to ensure complete submersion.
For same-day processing, incubate the tissue at 19°C-21°C with slow rotation of the tube for 3-4 hours.
Peel off the epidermis from the dermis after digestion in liberase.
Enzymatically digest and mechanically manipulate both layers to produce single cell suspensions.
Isolate keratinocytes and melanocytes from the epidermis, while fibroblasts, microvascular endothelial cells, and preadipocytes are isolated from the dermis.
Prepare three 6 cm dishes.
Add 5 mL of HBSS to one dish.
Add 3 mL of trypsin to another dish.
Leave the third dish empty.
Decant digested tissue pieces into the empty dish.
Take one piece of tissue at a time.
Hold the dermis with forceps.
Peel the epidermis layer off with another pair of forceps.
Place the epidermis in the dish containing trypsin.
Transfer the dermis to the dish containing HBSS.
When digestion is complete, pull gently from the corner to separate epidermis in one piece.
If necessary, continue incubation with liberase for another hour at 4 °C.
Use curved forceps to remove large floating pieces of epidermis by pulling and rubbing it on the bottom of the dish.
Incubate epidermis for 10 min at 19°C–21°C.
Place 2-3 pieces of dermis with de-epidermized side face down in a 10 cm uncoated plate.
Leave the dish open in the hood for about 15 min to dry slightly.
Add 1 ml of warm fibroblast medium supplemented with double concentration of antibiotics, almost covering tissue but not entirely floating it.
Carefully place the dish in the tissue culture incubator.
At the end of the day, add 4 ml of warm fibroblast medium supplemented with double concentration of antibiotics to the plate.
Place a piece of de-epidermized dermis side face down in gelatin-coated well of a 6-well plate.
Aspirate the gelatin from the plate before placing the tissue piece.
Leave the dish open for about 15 min to dry slightly and help attachment.
Add 0.25 ml of warm fibroblast medium supplemented with double concentration of antibiotics, focusing on the tissue piece.
Place the dish in the tissue culture incubator carefully.
At the end of the day, add 0.25 ml more of warm fibroblast medium supplemented with double concentration of antibiotics to the plate.
Mince remaining dermis pieces with scissors and transfer them into a tube with collagenase solution.
Digest dermis pieces in a 37 °C water bath with frequent agitation until completely digested (between 45 min and 1.5 h).
Incubate the mixture for about 30 minutes until a fat layer appears on top of the tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 250 g for 5 minutes at 19°C–21°C.
Aspirate the fat layer and supernatant together.
Add 2.5 mL of collagenase solution to the tissue pieces.
Continue digestion until tissue dissolves, avoiding incubation times exceeding 1.5 hours.
Add 3 mL of trypsin inhibitor to the digested epidermis.
Vigorously pipette the solution up and down with a 1 mL pipette tip to further dissociate single cells from the epidermis.
Split the digested epidermis into two 15 mL tubes.
Centrifuge at 250 g for 5 minutes at 19°C–21°C.
Aspirate collagen/fibronectin and gelatin solutions from coated vessels.
Remove supernatant from each 15 mL tube.
Resuspend the pellets by flicking the tubes a couple of times.
Add 10 mL of warm M2 medium supplemented with double concentration of antibiotics to one tube.
Add appropriate volume of warmed CnT supplemented with double concentration of antibiotics and 10 μM Y-27632 dihydrochloride to the second tube.
Seed resuspended melanocytes and keratinocytes into appropriate vessels.
Place the seeded cells in the incubator.
Once pieces of dermis are digested, add 9 mL HBSS to the tube.
Pass the cell suspension through a 70 μm cell strainer into a 50 mL tube.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 15 mL tube and centrifuge at 250 g for 5 minutes at 19°C–21°C.
Prepare six 5 mL FACS tubes, each containing 1 mL of warm ECMV medium.
Add between 2 and 5 μL of CD31 Dynabeads to the first tube based on tissue size.
Mix thoroughly and place the tube in a magnet stand for 1 minute to wash.
Aspirate media from washed beads when still on magnetic stand.
Add 1 mL of warm ECMV medium to the washed beads.
Remove supernatant from centrifuged cells, resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of warm ECMV medium.
Add cell suspension to the tube containing CD31 Dynabeads.
Securely replace cap and invert tube several times.
Place the tube on a roller at 7 rpm.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 19°C–21°C.
Briefly spin down the tube to collect all cells at the bottom of the tube when incubation is complete.
Remove the cap and place the tube in a magnet stand.
Allow beads to collect on magnet, turn the tube 180 degrees to release any trapped cells and leave for 2 minutes.
Collect the supernatant containing unbound cells into a fresh 15 mL tube while sitting on a magnet.
Take the tube out of the magnet and resuspend the beads in 1 mL of warm ECMV medium.
Transfer the cell supernatant into the next tube and place it on the magnetic stand.
Repeat steps until final tube is done, combining unbound cells from each step into the same 15 mL tube.
Aspirate gelatin coating solution from one of the coated vessels.

Resuspend purified CD31 positive microvascular endothelial cells in warm ECMV supplemented with double concentration of antibiotics and seed into appropriate gelatin-coated vessel based on tissue size.
Centrifuge the 15 mL tube with unbound cells for 5 min at 250 g at 19 °C–21°C.
Prepare six 5 mL FACS tubes, each with 1 mL of warm preadipocyte medium.
Add CD34 Dynabeads to the first tube based on tissue size and mix thoroughly.
Place in a magnet stand for 1 min to wash beads.
Aspirate media from washed beads while still on magnetic stand and add 1 mL of warm preadipocyte medium.
Remove supernatant from centrifuged cells, resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL of warm preadipocyte medium and add cell suspension to the tube with beads.
Securely replace cap, invert tube several times, place it on a roller at 7 rpm.
Incubate for 15 min at 19 °C–21°C.
Briefly spin down the tube to collect all cells at the bottom.
Remove the cap and place the tube in the magnet stand.
Allow beads to collect on magnet, turn the tube 180 degrees to release any cells trapped accidentally on the magnet, then let it sit for 2 minutes.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant containing unbound cells while the tube is sitting on a magnet, avoiding disturbing the beads.
Take the tube out of the magnet and resuspend the beads in 1 mL of warm preadipocyte medium.
Transfer the cell supernatant into the next tube and place it in the magnetic stand.
If tissue is too small to yield 3 pieces in step 4, collect the supernatant containing unbound cells into a 15 mL tube.
Take the tube out of the magnet and resuspend the beads in 1 mL of warm preadipocyte medium.
Transfer the cell supernatant into the next tube and place it in the magnetic stand.
Repeat steps 47 and 48 until all tubes are done, combining unbound cells from step 48b into the same 15 mL tube.
Aspirate gelatin coating solution from coated vessel.

Depending on tissue size, resuspend purified CD34 positive preadipocytes in 2 mL (for a 6-well plate), 5 mL (for a 6 cm plate) or 10 mL (for a T75 flask) of warm preadipocyte medium supplemented with double concentration of antibiotics.
Seed into the appropriate gelatin-coated vessel.
Centrifuge the tube with unbound cells from step 49 at 250 g for 5 minutes at 19 °C–21°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 2 mL of warm fibroblasts medium supplemented with double concentration of antibiotics for a 6-well plate.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of warm fibroblasts medium supplemented with double concentration of antibiotics for a 6 cm plate.
Seed into an appropriate gelatin-coated vessel.
Change media of all cell types to ones containing single concentration of antibiotics approximately 24 hours after cell isolation.
Avoid aspirating dermis pieces during media changes for the first couple of days after isolation.
Expand cells before freezing if they were seeded into a 6-well plate or 6 cm dish.
Change medium every other day, using single concentration of antibiotics for 7 days.
Grow cells without antibiotics after the initial 7-day period with antibiotics.
Pass confluent cells when necessary by coating appropriate vessels with suitable coating solution at 37 °C for at least 1 hour.
Wash cells once with HBSS before passing.
Add trypsin to detach cells: use 0.5 ml in a 6-well plate, 1 ml in a 6 cm plate, or 2 ml in a T75 flask.
Incubate fibroblasts and preadipocytes at 19 °C–21°C until they start rounding up.
Incubate keratinocytes at 37 °C for longer trypsinization to detach properly.
Add equal volume of trypsin inhibitor and transfer the cell suspension into a 15 mL tube.
Wash the dish once with HBSS to collect any cells left behind and add it to the same 15 mL tube.
Incubate melanocytes in 5 mL of HBSS for 10–20 min at 37 °C.
Knock the vessel forcefully to detach melanocytes from the vessel when they start to round up, then transfer supernatant to a 15 mL tube.
Wash the dish once with HBSS and add it to the same 15 mL tube.
Incubate melanocytes for 5 min at 37 °C in HBSS before scraping them using a cell scrapper.
Centrifuge the tube at 250 g for 5 min at 19–21°C, then aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend isolated cells in cold freezing mix at a concentration of 0.5–2 million cells per milliliter.
Aliquot 1 mL of cell suspension into each cryovial.
Place the cryovials in a freezing container and store at -80 °C for 24 hours.
Transfer the cryovials to liquid nitrogen storage after 24 hours.
